title: The rewiring of globalization is under way
gist: Hung Tran argues that globalization is being rewired rather than reversed: trade hit over 68 percent of GDP in 2025, driven by AI goods and critical minerals, even as trade and FDI fragment along geopolitical lines, with South-South trade rising and low-income countries hurt most.

insights.claim: Global trade rose to more than 68 percent of GDP in 2025 from around 60 percent in recent years, which contradicts the deglobalization narrative.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Aggregate trade intensity is rising; frame the shift as supply-chain reconfiguration.

insights.claim: Supply chains are being reconfigured toward resilience, replacing just-in-time efficiency with just-in-case inventory to manage disruption risk.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Higher inventory and redundancy costs support margins of suppliers of buffers but raise structural cost.
insights.locator: A rewiring of globalization essentially means

themes.theme: AI and critical minerals driving trade

insights.claim: AI-related goods account for 15 percent of merchandise trade but contributed 42 percent of trade growth in the first three quarters of 2026.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: AI capex is the main marginal driver of trade growth; AI cycle risk is trade risk.
insights.locator: Driving the recent growth in trade

insights.claim: Trade in critical minerals needed for semiconductors and other AI hardware has reached $2.5 trillion, about 10 percent of total merchandise trade.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Critical-mineral exporters benefit from AI and defense demand.
insights.locator: Driving the recent growth in trade

insights.claim: Services trade is growing 4.7 percent a year versus 2.2 percent for goods, lifting services to 25 percent of world trade, with cross-border data flows as lifeblood.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Structural shift toward digital services in trade.
insights.locator: In particular, cross-border trade or flow of data

themes.theme: Geopolitical fragmentation of trade and investment

insights.claim: Quarterly trade volumes grow about 2.5 percent more slowly between geopolitically distant countries than between aligned ones.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.locator: Changes in patterns of trade and investment

insights.claim: Investment share among geopolitically distant countries fell from 23 to 13 percent between 2013 and 2022, while flows among close advanced countries rose from 35 to 45 percent, which is friendshoring in practice.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Capital allocation favors geopolitically close destinations.
insights.locator: Changes in patterns of trade and investment

insights.claim: FDI rose 14 percent to $1.6 trillion in 2025, with flows to developed countries up 43 percent while flows to developing countries fell 2 percent, hitting low-income countries hardest.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Capital concentration in developed economies raises funding stress for the poorest countries.
insights.locator: This practice has costs for the developing world

insights.claim: US imports as a share of world imports fell from 14 percent in 2015 to about 13 percent, and its export share fell from 9 percent to about 8.5 percent, as other countries trade more with each other to adjust to unpredictable US tariffs.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: US tariffs are accelerating trade diversification away from the US.
insights.locator: Changes in the positions of US and China

insights.claim: Regional trade agreements notified to the WTO rose from 350 in 2022 to 580.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Proliferating plurilateral deals mark a reorienting trade architecture.
insights.locator: Changes in the positions of US and China

insights.claim: China's share of world trade rose from 4.4 percent in 2001 to 15 percent in 2020 and has hovered there; its foreign value-added content in exports fell from 19.4 to 17 percent from 2010 to 2022, suggesting Made in China 2025 largely achieved its aim.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: China is less dependent on foreign inputs and demand, reducing others' leverage.
insights.locator: By contrast, China has lifted its share

insights.claim: A rising Chinese trade surplus has led observers to coin China Shock 2.0, which the author calls a neo-mercantilist approach that is not equitable or sustainable.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Chinese surplus growth is a trade-policy flashpoint likely to draw more protectionist responses.

insights.claim: South-South trade is growing 8 to 9 percent annually to $7.2 trillion, 57 percent of developing-country goods exports, and Southeast Asia has become a hub in critical minerals and AI-related products such as semiconductors.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Emerging-market trade is decoupling from developed-market demand; Southeast Asia is a key beneficiary.

insights.claim: Asia is estimated to contribute about 68 percent of global GDP expansion in 2026.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Asia is the dominant growth driver for 2026.

insights.claim: Countries close to major powers and in AI and critical-mineral supply chains fare better, while low-income countries suffer sluggish trade, FDI declines and cuts to official development aid.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Divergence between integrated and excluded economies raises sovereign stress risk in low-income countries.
